newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Russia firms borrowing plans for 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia firms borrowing plans for 1997-98.

text.p: Russia will borrow up to $3.5 billion from international bond markets this year and raise $3.0-3.5 billion in 1998, Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Friday.
"That is an appropriate amount for us using this source of funding," Kasyanov told a news conference, although the domestic market would remain Russia's main source of funding.
Russian officials were in London to meet investors ahead of Moscow's next Eurobond issue, due next week. Kasyanov said the deal would likely be a 10-year transaction worth at least $1.0 billion.
Kasyanov said Russia would complete its borrowing for 1997 with a global dollar bond offer in the autumn. Its prior deal this year was a 2.0 billion mark ($1.2 billion) seven-year financing in March.
Looking ahead, Kasyanov said: "We are seriously considering a yen deal for 1998. It is an important currency."
But he played down the possibility of a rouble Eurobond in the near term, saying: "Such speculation is premature. But we will rule nothing out."
The idea of a rouble Eurobond was floated by former finance minister Alexander Livshits earlier this year, just days before he was sacked.
Modern Russia's international borrowing programme began last November with a $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond.
Since that deal and the mark bond, two Russian borrowers -- the cities of Moscow and St Petersburg -- have tapped the market. A host of other names are in the process of lining up deals.
Kasyanov said there was no cap on Russian deals but that it would analyse the situation later this year.

"We will look at the market more closely in two months after the (upcoming Eurobond) issue. We will talk to lead managers to see what level (of issuance) is acceptable to investors so the Russian share of the market is appropriate. It would be premature to do so now."
Kasyanov said the two Eurobonds issued so far by Russia had helped Russia's macro-economic situation. "They have helped press internal rates down."

Roadshows for Russia's upcoming Eurobond end on June 18 after sarting on Wednesday. "On the basis of our analysis of market reception we are looking for a 10-year term and a size of not less than $1.0 billion," Kasyanov said.

J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg are joint lead managers for the transaction. London-based bankers said this week that a 10-year Russian Eurobond could be priced to yield around 375 basis points, or 3.75 percentage points, over U.S. Treasury notes.
